node-1.label: Patient presented with tension-like headaches for several months

node-2.label: Male veteran in his 40s with a history of posttraumatic stress disorder, traumatic brain injury, and chronic headaches; had undergone tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy in childhood; no sinonasal symptoms, radiation exposure, or trauma.

node-3.label: The headaches were unrelieved by medical treatment.

node-4.label: Head and neck examination including flexible nasopharyngolaryngoscopy showed bilateral fullness of the nasopharynx, with submucosal lesions appearing to be within the torus tubarii.

why.why: Pathology, the gold standard, shows benign respiratory mucosa with reactive lymphoid hyperplasia and chronic inflammation, and all three experts interpret the culture, purulence, and restricted diffusion as infectious/inflammatory rather than neoplastic. Confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.03.

Pathologist, Radiologist, and Laboratory Physician analyses all independently conclude that benign respiratory mucosa with reactive lymphoid hyperplasia, chronic inflammation, S. lugdunensis growth, endoscopic purulence, and MRI restricted diffusion coherently support an infectious/inflammatory nasopharyngeal lesion and exclude neoplasm. This cross-specialty consensus raises confidence from 0.9 to 0.93; absent sinonasal symptoms and missing contrast MRI/IHC/EBV DNA are limitations but do not override the convergent objective findings.

The pathologist, radiologist, and laboratory physician all agree that the objective nasopharyngeal inflammatory/infectious findings provide a structural explanation for the treatment-resistant headaches, making primary/post-traumatic headache unlikely. Confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.03.

node-8.label: MRI shows bilateral nasopharyngeal lesions with restricted diffusion

node-9.label: Endoscopy reveals enlarged cystic torus tubarius with purulence after biopsy

node-10.label: Pathology demonstrates benign respiratory mucosa with reactive lymphoid hyperplasia and mild chronic inflammation

node-12.label: Patient has infectious/inflammatory nasopharyngeal lesion caused by Staphylococcus lugdunensis

why.why: All three experts agree that culture growing S. lugdunensis, benign reactive pathology, endoscopic purulence, and MRI restricted diffusion coherently explain the treatment-resistant headaches as an infectious/inflammatory nasopharyngeal lesion caused by S. lugdunensis. Confidence is raised from 0.85 to 0.9; lack of follow-up imaging and absent sinonasal symptoms are acknowledged but the microbiological and pathological evidence is strong.

node-13.label: Patient has an infected nasopharyngeal cyst/abscess caused by Staphylococcus lugdunensis

attrs.why: Endoscopy revealed an enlarged cystic torus tubarius with purulence after biopsy, MRI showed restricted diffusion consistent with pus/infection, and culture grew S. lugdunensis. These findings support an infected cystic/abscess lesion as a specific form of the benign/inflammatory nasopharyngeal lesion. Confidence is 0.6 because pathology did not explicitly confirm a cyst wall or abscess cavity and no follow-up imaging is available.
